Core Concepts

What turn, blueprint, constraint, and tripwire mean in AFWE ReBorn, and how each compares to the meaning you already know.

❝
Graph tools tell the agent what your code is. AFWE tells it what your code is supposed to be, and refuses changes that break that.

Turns: where intent meets reality Protocol

Delta organizes work into threads. In AFWE, every prompt is a Turn. AFWE never runs the agent loop or calls an LLM internally: the harness (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) is the model, and AFWE is the deterministic verification kernel.

Every turn is structured into an atomic 3-step loop:

STEP 1
turn begin

Gathers briefing: scoped nodes, active pins, living intents, and registered checks.

STEP 2
turn assume

Agent declares intents and AST claims before editing any source code.

STEP 3
turn commit

Deterministic gating: checks AST claims, collateral losses, constraints, and pins.

Interactive Turn Receipt:
Turn #482 2026-10-25 14:32:00 UTC
Developer Prompt

"Refactor checkout flow to support guest payments without touching core auth"

Claims (Declared) 4/4 verified
  • ✓ No features removed
  • ✓ Checkout still works (unit tests)
  • ✓ AST Export: process_guest_payment
  • ✓ Comments blanked (zero regex false pos)
Checks (Deterministic) 3/3 passed
  • ✓ Constraints passed (must_not_depend UI)
  • ✓ Pins respected (Auth locked)
  • ✓ Collateral loss: 0 undeclared
COMMIT All claims verified & boundaries preserved.
Trailer: AFWE-Turn: 482

The Blueprint: what code is supposed to be Scene Graph

Delta has projects. AFWE has the Blueprint (.afwe/blueprint/blueprint.yaml). The blueprint is a deterministic hierarchical AST scene graph representing structural reality:

  • Product ➔ Subsystems ➔ Modules ➔ Components: Every file and symbol resolves to exactly one node (or surfaces as unmapped drift).
  • Purpose Mapping: Records why each component exists. When an agent touches code, it receives this intent as micro-context.
  • Active Pins: Human-locked decisions (intentional bugs, keep it like that) that autonomous refactors cannot touch.

Constraints are Geometry Active Gating

Architecture rules are not vague prose suggestions in markdown files that LLMs conveniently forget when context fills up. In AFWE, constraints are geometry. If an agent adds an import that violates a declared boundary (must_not_depend), the turn gate refuses the commit immediately.

Constraints are Geometry Active Kernel Gate

"If an arrow points the wrong way, you see it instantly."

Allowed Flow
Blocking Violation
Locked Pin
Gate Status: REFUSES COMMIT (exit code 1)

Tripwires: where boundaries are guarded Materialize

Delta has worktrees. AFWE has Tripwires & Materialization. When you run afwe materialize --apply, AFWE generates zero-overhead, tamper-proof architectural tripwires:

1. .afwe/guardrails/manifest.yaml (BLAKE3)

Cryptographic BLAKE3 manifest of all guardrails. CI compares PRs against the protected base branch manifest to prevent agents from silently deleting guardrails.

2. Chained Pre-Commit Git Hook

Executes fast verification locally while preserving existing Husky or Python pre-commit hooks.

3. GitHub Actions CI Gate

Runs afwe materialize --check --base origin/main to block non-compliant PRs.

Probing Guides & Calibration Rubric Anti-Echo Chamber

In ReBorn, confidence is calculated from an additive deterministic rubric, never from raw LLM floats:

Base Rubric Floor 0.50
+ High-quality AST/symbol/import claim +0.25
+ Consistent with sibling modules under same subsystem +0.10
+ Qualifying probes across distinct sessions (max 5) +0.02 each
Contradiction with active pin or prior answer CAPS AT 0.40

Inferred rules with confidence between 0.85 and 0.90 become Probing Guides ([GUIDE - ADVISORY]). They guide the agent without blocking commits. To graduate to a blocking check, AFWE requires at least 1 hold-out probe turn (where the rule was deliberately withheld from context and the invariant was still preserved).

Explore Mode & Authority Spikes

Strict constraints are essential for shipping production code, but during early research or architectural spikes, you want velocity.

afwe unlock --reason "..."

Activates Explore Mode: blocking checks and constraints downgrade to advisory warnings.

afwe lock

Re-arms the deterministic gate, enforcing leaf-to-root TurnJudgment verification.

4D Timeline: time as a dial DOTS Engine

Git commits tell you which files changed. AFWE's 4D timeline tells you which features evolved, appeared, or disappeared.

If an agent inadvertently removes a feature during a refactor, AFWE displays it as a ghost node on the timeline. Restoring it is a single command:

afwe timeline restore guest-checkout --apply

AFWE performs a true 3-way merge against the last good commit, opens a new turn, and stages the restoration cleanly.

How They Fit Together Unified System

Code knowledge graphing, intent memory, and tripwires are not separate tools; they form a single continuous architectural feedback loop:

The 5 Architectural Layers Unified Truth

Same truth. Different views. One system.
Layer 5
Receipts

What happened. Append-only log of every change, signed claims, and gate decisions.

log/ & turns/*.yaml
Layer 4
Timeline

When it happened. 4D dial scrubber across turns. Restores features via 3-way merge.

afwe timeline restore
Layer 3
Graph

How it's connected. AST scene graph, directional dependencies, and geometric constraints.

constraints.yaml
Layer 2
Blueprint

What it is. Nested parcels of subsystems and modules mapped to physical source files.

blueprint.yaml
Layer 1
Features

Your product. User-facing capabilities, intents, and business deliverables.

intents/*.yaml
